English: Spindle Patch
A simple clearing where nomads gather to twist fibers into rough thread, marking the beginnings of textile craft among the tribe.
Weavers Tent
A basic tent of woven grass, where skilled hands begin to organize and produce simple cloth for the tribes needs.
Loom Hut
A wooden structure fitted with primitive looms, improving the tribes ability to create more varied and durable fabrics.
Dye Pavilion
A gathering of covered stalls for dyeing fabrics with natural colors, adding value and distinction to tribal textiles.
Patterned Room
A large, semi-permanent structure devoted to creating intricate woven patterns, symbolizing the tribes cultural identity.
Textile Chamber
A well-defended, multi-purpose workshop where master weavers oversee advanced textile production and train apprentices.
Market Weaver Hall
A bustling hall at the heart of the camp, where textiles are traded and new designs fetch high prices from passing merchants.
Guild Pavilion
A grand pavilion for the weavers’ guild, regulating trade, ensuring quality, and fostering unity among the tribes artisans.
Master Weavers Room
A private chamber for the master of the guild, where the most intricate and prized textiles are woven, inspiring the entire clan.
Central African Weaving Guild
The pinnacle of nomadic textile culture: a permanent, legendary guild complex drawing artisans from all tribes, fueling prosperity and unity.
